projects.title: Pawffice
projects.tagline: Multiplayer 3D cat office: one three.js engine in a Tauri Mac app and an Expo Android app
projects.summary: A local-first, multi-agent AI workspace for the desktop, presented as a 3D town where a crew of cats takes your prompts.
highlights: Classifies each prompt into ordered AI stages and feeds every stage the previous one's output
Pricing gates before anything runs, repository-path isolation and rate-limit handling
13 P0 build-blocking tests guard the cost and security rules

engineering.architecture: Dependencies point one way: phone, then desktop page, then engine. packages/cattown is a three.js engine whose rules (steering, physics, driving, network smoothing) sit in pure, unit-tested modules. The Pawffice page, plain JavaScript, mounts it and reaches its host through one ipc module: Tauri commands into Rust on the Mac, a swapped shim on the phone, where an Expo shell runs the page in a WebView. Supabase provides accounts and Realtime.

decisions.title: One engine, never a second
decisions.detail: The phone is an Expo/React Native shell around a WebView running the desktop page, rebuilt with esbuild and one swapped ipc module. A native 3D rewrite needs a new ADR; the build fails if Tauri code leaks in.

decisions.title: The API token never reaches the page
decisions.detail: Rust seals the Claude token with AES-256-GCM under an Argon2id key (64 MiB, 3 passes). It lives only in the Rust process, zeroized on sign-out; the web page gets back name and role only.

decisions.title: Shared NPCs with no game server
decisions.detail: Clients elect one NPC host from Realtime presence (oldest join wins), so every device agrees without a server. The host sends 4 delta frames a second to stay under Supabase's free-plan message quota; lockstep was rejected.

decisions.title: A measured phone quality tier
decisions.detail: Phones get 8 fur shells instead of 16, a 1024² shadow map and a 30 fps idle cap. Measured: about 44 to 36 ms per frame and 1.57M to 0.77M triangles; desktop unchanged.

projects.title: BubuProtect
projects.tagline: On-device Android password vault with layered encryption and a device threat shield
projects.summary: An Android password vault that keeps logins, cards, notes, ID documents and Wi-Fi keys encrypted on the device, behind a master passphrase.
highlights: Encrypted on-device vault (Room over SQLCipher) for five kinds of secret, with FLAG_SECURE and tap-jacking defences
Live TOTP codes with a countdown ring, and a breach check that sends only a 5-character hash prefix
Device check: 10 local probes, from debugging switches to network interception, each linked to its setting

engineering.architecture: Single Gradle module: ui (Compose screens, StateFlow ViewModels), domain (models, VaultRepository interface), data (Room DAOs over SQLCipher), session (holds keys and the open database only while unlocked), and core feature packages for crypto, autofill, security probes, shield, OTP, backup and import. Koin wires it. No backend; the one network call is a k-anonymous Pwned Passwords lookup.

decisions.title: One key, three independent locks
decisions.detail: A 256-bit root key is wrapped by a hardware Keystore key (biometric per use, destroyed if a new fingerprint is enrolled), by PBKDF2-SHA512 at 210k iterations, and by a paper recovery code, so no single failure loses the vault.

decisions.title: Two encryption layers, bound per field
decisions.detail: SQLCipher encrypts the database file; AES-GCM then seals each credential column with the entry id and column name as associated data, so copied or swapped ciphertext fails as tampering instead of leaking.

decisions.title: Locked means the keys are gone
decisions.detail: On lock, VaultSession closes the database, zeroes the derived passphrase and wipes the root key, so a locked vault cannot be read from a heap dump. Re-entry needs real authentication.

decisions.title: DNS-only VPN for ad tracking
decisions.detail: The VpnService routes a single /32 fake DNS address, so only DNS enters the tunnel: no userspace TCP stack, other traffic never touched, and no way to carry user traffic anywhere.

projects.title: Vistago
projects.tagline: Offline-first AI travel companion for Android with a self-healing free-LLM model router
projects.summary: An offline-first AI travel companion for Android: plan trips, translate through the camera, and keep travel memories, with or without a connection.
highlights: 12 feature areas, 16 screens, about 450 composables in 366 Kotlin files
OpenRouter model routing with live discovery, role-based pinning, cooldowns and availability tracking
Falls back to on-device processing when LLM services fail

engineering.architecture: Single Gradle module layered as Compose UI, then 16 ViewModels exposing StateFlow and sealed UI states, then a pure-Kotlin domain layer (models, repository interfaces, use cases, LLM routing rules; zero android imports), then a data layer (Room, OpenRouter, ML Kit, Supabase, WorkManager). Koin wires the graph and injects a named IO dispatcher. Room is the source of truth; Supabase is optional best-effort sync behind the same interfaces.

decisions.title: Self-healing model router
decisions.detail: No model is hard-coded. The router discovers free OpenRouter models at call time, benches a model for a cooldown after a 429, treats retired models as a reroute, and tags every reply with which model answered.

decisions.title: Degrades instead of breaking
decisions.detail: Koin picks implementations at startup: without an API key, trip planning and interest suggestions fall back to on-device versions, and live camera translation runs entirely on device with ML Kit, so the app stays usable offline.

decisions.title: Local-first data, swappable remote
decisions.detail: Room owns the experience offline, at schema v12 with 11 explicit migrations and no destructive fallback. Supabase sync and an Edge Function proxy sit behind repository interfaces so AI secrets never ship in the APK.

decisions.title: Release safety in the build
decisions.detail: R8 is on for release with minimal keep rules. Release tasks fail without a usable signing key instead of silently using the debug key, and secrets reach only debug builds by default.

projects.title: Calm Escape Premier
projects.tagline: Multi-tenant spa booking: KMP apps and Next.js sites on one database-enforced schedule
projects.summary: A multi-tenant booking platform for spas: each spa gets its own booking site and staff back office, customers book from iOS and Android apps, and all of them share one schedule.
highlights: No double booking, even under races: Postgres exclusion constraints, covered by 184 pgTAP tests (plus 346 Vitest tests on the web)
One codebase serves every spa: its own subdomain or domain, server-rendered, in one of three designs
Staff back office with monthly sales, a menu and membership editor, and promo bundles with a live phone and web preview

engineering.architecture: Two thin front ends over one database. Tenant isolation (Row Level Security), double-booking prevention (exclusion constraints), slot availability and booking and voucher RPCs live once in Postgres, so Kotlin and TypeScript cannot disagree. mobile/shared holds models, supabase-kt repositories, ViewModels with StateFlow and the Compose UI for Android and iOS. Next.js routes by host and server-renders cached spa pages. Dependencies are passed by constructor; no DI framework.

decisions.title: Business rules live in Postgres
decisions.detail: Mobile is Kotlin and web is TypeScript, so availability, booking, cancellation and voucher rules are SQL functions over RPC and access is RLS. Both clients only render and call the same functions, with stable error hints.

decisions.title: Double-booking impossible, even under races
decisions.detail: EXCLUDE USING gist constraints on bookings stop a therapist or room being booked twice at the database. Voucher claim limits are enforced inside a claim_voucher RPC; customers cannot write claims directly.

decisions.title: Tenant-safe foreign keys
decisions.detail: Every spa-owned row carries tenant_id, and child rows reference parents by composite (id, tenant_id) keys, so a booking cannot point at another spa's service, therapist, room or location.

decisions.title: KMP for apps, server-rendered web
decisions.detail: The team knows Kotlin, so apps are KMP + Compose Multiplatform. Flutter and Compose for web draw to a canvas with weak SEO, so spa sites are server-rendered Next.js (ADR 0001).

projects.summary: An inventory and dealer-floor app for a Makati art gallery, built once in Compose Multiplatform for Android, iOS and the web. Runs on sample data while the data layer is built.
highlights: Painterly splash: 900 strokes follow a flow field and converge onto the logo's own pixels (260 on the web)
Home tuned to the frame budget: figures and sparkline animate only in view; skeletons animate in the draw phase

engineering.architecture: A KMP library, :shared, holds every screen in commonMain; :androidApp, :webApp (Wasm and JS) and an Xcode iosApp are thin entry points. Each screen splits into a stateless Content composable, a thin Screen wrapper and a multiplatform ViewModel exposing StateFlow of a sealed UiState. Platform differences go through expect/actual. Data is sample and in-memory for now; DI and a database are planned, not built.

decisions.title: One UI codebase, no Android leaks
decisions.detail: commonMain has zero android.* imports. Platform needs such as reduced motion are expect/actual with Android, iOS, JS and Wasm implementations, so all three apps run the same UI code.

decisions.title: Reflection-free navigation
decisions.detail: Destinations are a @Serializable sealed interface on Navigation 3 with explicit polymorphic serializers, because reflection is unavailable on iOS and Wasm and the back stack must still restore there.

decisions.title: Animation budgeted per platform
decisions.detail: The 900-stroke painterly splash plays once per process on Android and iOS only. It is skipped on the web, on warm start and under reduced motion, because that many canvas strokes would stall a browser tab.

decisions.title: State modelled before the data source
decisions.detail: ViewModels emit sealed UiState from sample data, with optimistic updates, so a future injected use case can replace the sample without touching the UI layer.

projects.title: This portfolio
projects.tagline: One Compose UI compiled to WebAssembly, with crawlable HTML built from the same JSON
projects.summary: A Compose Multiplatform app running in your browser through Kotlin/WebAssembly, with a crawlable HTML version generated from the same content at build time.
highlights: Adaptive layout from phone to wide desktop using window size classes
Content lives in one JSON file shared by the app and the generated HTML
Built, tested and deployed to GitHub Pages by GitHub Actions

engineering.architecture: One Gradle module in one-way layers: UI, ViewModel, repository, parser, model. All content is one JSON file, validated by the same parser in the app and in the build task that renders the crawlable HTML. The browser paints that HTML first, loads the Wasm app behind it and swaps to the canvas once Compose has drawn; a small hash router gives every project its own link.

decisions.title: Crawlable HTML first, canvas second
decisions.detail: A canvas is invisible to search engines and screen readers, and the runtime is megabytes. The build renders the same JSON to HTML, which paints first and stays the page where WasmGC is missing.

decisions.title: Clips decoded one frame at a time
decisions.detail: Skia's Codec decodes animated WebP into one reusable bitmap inside the frame clock: about 1.2 MB a clip instead of 28 MB, and a shared gate allows one decode per display frame.

decisions.title: Content mistakes fail the build
decisions.detail: The app's parser also runs in Gradle, and tests check every listed image against its budget, so a broken link, missing alt text, an oversized image or a module cycle stops the deploy.

decisions.title: A hand-rolled router, no library
decisions.detail: Two screens do not need a navigation library: an expect/actual navigator keeps #/projects/<id> links and browser Back on the web, and a plain back stack on the desktop.
